report:
The retained-endpoint theorem is established. This verdict concerns precisely endpoints T and D in the task; it does not close the original arbitrary-field catalogue atom. The author’s partial status and candidate flag do not determine this verdict.

I checked the indispensable statements in the exact primary versions 1201.0187v2, 1201.0188v1, 1805.01016v3, 1801.08229v4 and 2307.01697v1. I also opened the published BGM22 paper and checked its Lemma 3.2. The smooth geometrically integral variety in D satisfies the geometrically reduced hypothesis needed by BE and BGM. BFJ’s v1 Theorem A genuinely retains algebraizability and SNC-support assumptions. The argument correctly uses the broader operator and potential-theory results, and separately proves the passages replacing those two restrictions.

The intersection measure is genuine: its model coefficients are b_E(ℒ|E)^n, and their sum is V. Positive real scaling gives M_{λθ}(λu)=λ^nM_θ(u) and E_{λθ}(λu)=λE_θ(u). Thus λ=V^(−1/n) legitimately applies BFJ’s unit-volume statements without changing the raw equation or restricting the target.

For D, bounded locality makes the restricted measures 1_{u>−t}M_θ(max(u,−t)) compatible and increasing. Integer truncation levels are cofinal. Their finite increasing limit is Radon: inner regularity follows by approximating first with one restricted measure and then with a compact subset. The bounded energy difference formula yields t·m_θ(u_t){u≤−t}≤2(n+1)[E_θ(u_{t/2})−E_θ(u_t)]→0. This proves the required o(1/t) discarded mass and exact mass V. The truncation estimate is uniform along decreasing approximations whose limiting energy is finite; bounded decreasing continuity then proves finite-energy decreasing continuity and approximation independence.

The direct proof (7a)–(7b) is correct. For nonpositive u,v, positivity gives m((u_t+v_s)/2)≥2^(−n)m(u_t). Multiplying this measure inequality by a nonpositive function reverses the inequality, exactly as required. The bounded energy formula consequently gives E((u+v)/2)≤2^(−n−1)/(n+1)·∫_{u>−t}v_s dm(u). First increasing s and then t through integers is legitimate sequential monotone convergence. The resulting bound ∫v dm(u)≥(n+1)2^(n+1)E((u+v)/2)>−∞ establishes integrability. It does not use the erroneous positive integral in the printed v1 Lemma 6.10.

The mixed calculus also survives this correction. Polarization of MA of convex combinations gives positive mixed measures of the correct mixed intersection mass. The coefficients are limits of the bounded mixed coefficients, so they are independent of approximation. A mixed measure is dominated by a constant times MA of an average of its potentials; (7b) supplies finite-energy integrability. Polarizing the energy and passing decreasing majorants through the Radon lemma establishes the mixed pairing, integration by parts and the correctly signed Dirichlet Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. Segment energies have degree at most n+1, and coefficient convergence proves segment differentiation. Locality and full mass give finite-energy comparison.

I checked the uniqueness application beyond its theorem label. With ρ=u−v, the mixed Dirichlet argument gives −∫ρ dd^cρ∧θ^(n−1)≤C[∫(v−u)(m(u)−m(v))]^(2^(1−n)). Equal MA therefore gives zero Dirichlet pairing against every model test. After a bounded model reference change to a relatively ample determination, the vertical intersection matrix has nonnegative off-diagonal weights and zero weighted row sums. Its quadratic form is minus a sum of weighted squared differences of vertex values. Connectedness of the special fiber therefore makes ρ constant on its vertices. On models dominating a fixed model these constants agree at a retained divisorial point. Divisorial determination of psh functions gives global constancy. This avoids relying on the printed assertion that equal supremums automatically remain equal after subtracting the same nonconstant reference potential.

The orthogonality transfer is valid. Rational semipositive tests are uniformly dense. Maxima, or rational approximations followed by a sufficiently small upward shift, make the tests strictly below an obstacle directed. BFJ’s continuous envelope and decreasing model regularization provide tests strictly below f uniformly arbitrarily close to P_θ(f). Every sufficiently late member of the directed net lies between such a test and P_θ(f); hence the entire net converges uniformly. Synthetic Example 2.20 applies to this ordered net. BE’s continuous operator agrees with the model intersection operator and passes it to the limit. This proves classical orthogonality for model obstacles. Uniform density, the envelope Lipschitz estimate and continuous-MA convergence extend it to every continuous obstacle.

All antecedents of BFJ Corollary 7.3 are consequently established. Its unbounded proof uses decreasing model regularization, decreasing energy and MA continuity, and dominated convergence in its integral identity. Continuity of the integrand at zero can also be checked directly: for a positive parameter, subtract inf f so that the envelope family decreases to u as the parameter decreases to zero; adding constants does not change MA. Apply the same argument to −f for the negative parameter. Thus the required two-sided envelope derivative is genuinely available for unbounded finite-energy u.

The crucial arbitrary-measure pairing argument is complete. Finite Q first gives E¹-integrability and equality of the test and E¹ dual supremums. Decreasing model majorants have energies converging to E(u), while their target integrals have a uniform lower bound E(a)−Q. BFJ’s Radon/usc decreasing-net lemma, rather than an invalid general-net monotone-convergence assertion, passes this bound and the dual inequality to u.

For maximizing tests τ_j, synthetic coercivity bounds J(τ_j), and r_ν(τ_j)→0. In (2.27), take the second potential to be zero. Quasi-symmetry identifies its J(a,0) with a comparable quantity to the manuscript’s J(a)=J(0,a). Choosing R to bound Q(ν), J(τ_j) and J(a) gives the uniform estimate |∫a(dν−dm(τ_j))|≤C_R√r_ν(τ_j). For an E¹ potential, decreasing model majorants have converging energies and m₀-integrals, hence converging J. Eventually they lie in the R+1 set. The Radon-net lemma passes both integrals to the limit, establishing the same uniform estimate on the entire E¹ set with bounded J.

If u_i→u in BFJ’s psh topology, m₀ has finite divisorial support, so its pairing is continuous. Energy upper semicontinuity makes J lower semicontinuous and puts a J-bounded limit in E¹. Each fixed m(τ_j) also has finite divisorial support. These continuous pairings approximate the ν-pairing uniformly on the bounded-J set, proving convergence of the ν-integrals. For w_i=max(u_i,u), divisorial convergence gives w_i→u. Supremums and m₀-integrals are eventually bounded, and monotonicity bounds E(w_i) below; therefore J(w_i) is eventually bounded. Applying pairing convergence to both nets and using |u_i−u|=2w_i−u_i−u proves L¹ convergence. Every step applies to nets and hence to the compactness subnet used in existence.

The converse integrability criterion is also valid. Failure of a uniform integral bound on normalized tests with J≤1 produces the decreasing convex series Σ2^(−j)a_j with energy bounded below by −(1+T). Its m₀-integral prevents an identically −∞ limit. Decreasing energy continuity puts the limit in E¹, while sequential monotone convergence makes its ν-integral −∞, a contradiction. The quadratic scaling estimate J(ta)≤C_nt²J(a) then gives −∫a dν≤A(1+√(C_nJ(a))). Since normalized tests satisfy E(a)≤−J(a), the dual supremum is finite.

Existence is actual attainment in the potential space. A normalized model maximizing sequence has bounded J and energy. BFJ compactness supplies a psh subnet limit; energy upper semicontinuity and the proved pairing continuity show that this limit achieves Q. For v_t=P_θ(u+tf), the usc obstacle property gives v_t≤u+tf, while v_t≥u−|t|‖f‖∞ ensures finite energy. Maximality yields E(v_t)−E(u)≤t∫f dν. Dividing for both signs of t and using the unbounded envelope derivative gives m_θ(u)=ν on all continuous tests, hence M_θ(u)=μ as Radon measures. No support hypothesis enters.

Conversely, full mass, (7b), concavity and segment differentiation show Q(m(u))=E(u)−∫u dm(u)<∞; decreasing majorants establish equality with the test supremum. Constants force the raw mass to be V. Together with comparison and uniqueness, this proves the exact claimed range and bijection modulo constants.

Endpoint T is independently supported by the trivial-field source. The energy pairing is extended by decreasing majorants, is finite on finite-energy tuples, and defines the mixed measure by a positive functional on uniformly dense PL tests. Its value on constants gives the raw intersection mass. The weighted decreasing convergence needed in locality is Proposition 7.21(ii); it permits passing the model locality identity to finite-energy potentials. Comparison then follows from locality and full mass. Smoothness and characteristic zero supply envelopes and normalized compactness. Quantitative mixed estimates provide bounded-J pairing continuity; the convex-series argument gives the integrability characterization. Envelope differentiation, compactness and pairing continuity prove attainment and the equation, while the MA embedding gives uniqueness. Thus the use of Theorems 12.8–12.9 is supported by their dependencies rather than inferred from completeness of measures.

The reference cocycle has the stated signs. For bounded model h with θ′=θ+dd^ch semipositive, model intersection identities give M_{θ′}(u−h)=M_θ(u) and E_{θ′}(u−h)=E_θ(u)−E_θ(h). Translated decreasing majorants establish the unbounded identities. Translating the test cones gives Q_{θ′}(ν)=Q_θ(ν)+∫h dν−E_θ(h), and multiplying by V gives the raw formula. All correction terms are finite.

Harmless corrections must be recorded. A convergent net has eventually bounded supremums; the argument should discard an initial tail. BFJ’s segment polynomial degree is at most n+1, not the printed n. Its mixed polarization uses the interior indices 1,…,n−1 after subtracting the endpoint terms, and its Dirichlet square roots require negative self-pairings. In the trivial-field locality proof, the printed cross-reference to Proposition 7.19(iii) should point to weighted decreasing convergence, Proposition 7.21(ii). The printed absolute-value identity in Proposition 9.19 has a wrong sign; the manuscript’s identity 2max(u_i,u)−u_i−u is correct. These corrections leave the supplied proof strategy and hypotheses intact. The Lemma 6.10 sign error is handled by the manuscript’s explicit proof, not silently corrected and imported.

All four actual notes were audited with their stated support edges. n1 correctly distinguishes source domains and separates provenance from mathematics. n2’s T theorem is established. n3’s D deduction is established, including its previously essential test-to-E¹ passage. n4’s mathematical scope statement correctly leaves general nondiscrete fields unresolved. Its compilation, hash and execution claims are supplied artifact records; I did not independently rerun those checks. They are not premises of either endpoint theorem. The support graph is acyclic and no note supplies an otherwise missing mathematical assumption.

The splitlines/form-feed and LF location schemes must remain distinct. The numeric-range discrepancy does not defeat the theorem applications: the indispensable statements were located in the exact primary PDFs independently of those range labels. I could not independently re-render the supplied inspection images because web screenshots were unavailable. The retrieved source text and the supplied rendered-page evidence are consistent; moreover, the two-sided estimate needed from (2.27) is independently recoverable by exchanging its two test potentials and using quasi-symmetry. Neither uncertain image access nor unrepeated artifact checks leave an indispensable mathematical premise unresolved.

No completeness of potentials, unbounded operator, or surjectivity over general nondiscrete fields has been inferred from synthetic measure completeness. Original catalogue closure remains a separate question; the referenced original catalogue clauses are not established by the candidate flag or by this retained-endpoint proof.

passages.statement: For a smooth connected projective variety over a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, and a closed real model (1,1)-form θ of ample numerical class, BFJ’s θ-psh cone is convex and stable under constants and maxima; divisorial evaluations determine its elements; its topology is pointwise convergence on divisorial points, equivalently uniform convergence on SNC dual complexes; u↦sup(u−ψ) is continuous and proper for every model ψ; normalized PSH is compact; decreasing nontrivial limits remain psh; every psh function has decreasing psh model regularization; continuous obstacles have continuous psh envelopes. On sufficiently high models, a bounded model change makes θ relatively ample, with arbitrarily small change when θ is semipositive. BFJ, 1201.0187v2, Propositions 5.2 and 7.4–7.9, Theorems 7.10–7.11, 8.3 and 8.7.

For a smooth connected projective variety over a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, semipositive real model forms have symmetric positive mixed intersection measures, of their mixed numerical intersection mass, with model coefficients b_E times the special-fiber intersections. Integration by parts and Dirichlet seminegativity hold. For a semipositive model reference θ of ample class, the bounded mixed MA operator uniquely extends these measures continuously along decreasing bounded psh nets and satisfies bounded locality. Normalized intersection energy extends by psh model majorants, is concave, monotone, upper semicontinuous and decreasing-continuous, and satisfies the bounded energy difference and derivative identities. BFJ, 1201.0188v1, Propositions 2.19–2.21, Theorem 3.1, Theorem 5.1 and Propositions 6.1–6.3.

For a smooth connected projective variety over a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, with semipositive model reference θ of ample class, the restricted-truncation MA operator on E¹ satisfies finite-energy locality and comparison; mixed finite-energy calculus and differentiation of energy along psh segments hold; two E¹ potentials with equal MA differ by a constant. These statements require neither orthogonality, function-field algebraizability nor a target-support restriction. BFJ, 1201.0188v1, Propositions 6.11–6.12 and 8.2.

For a smooth connected projective variety over a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, let ω be a semipositive real model form of ample class with (ωⁿ)=1. If ∫(f−Pω(f))MA(Pω(f))=0 for every continuous f, then Eω∘Pω is Gâteaux differentiable on continuous obstacles. For every u∈E¹ and continuous f, Pω(u+tf) belongs to E¹ for all real t and its energy derivative at t=0 equals ∫f MA(u). BFJ, 1201.0188v1, Theorem 7.2 and Corollary 7.3.
passages.quote: Assume that ω has the orthogonality property.

passages.statement: On a compact Hausdorff space, integration against a finite positive Radon measure commutes with a pointwise decreasing net of upper semicontinuous functions bounded above, with the integral of the limit allowed to equal −∞. BFJ, 1201.0188v1, Lemma 2.23.
passages.quote: a decreasing net of usc functions on X

passages.statement: Over a complete valued field, on a geometrically reduced projective scheme, every psh metric on a semiample Q-line bundle is psh-regularizable. The mixed MA operator on continuous psh-regularizable metrics uniquely extends the smooth operator, is continuous from uniform convergence of metrics to weak convergence of Radon measures, and agrees for non-Archimedean model metrics with the model intersection measure. Boucksom–Eriksson, 1805.01016v3, Theorems 7.14, 8.4 and 8.18.

On a geometrically reduced projective scheme over any complete valued field, for continuous psh metrics φ and ψ on an ample line bundle L, the relative volume equals their relative intersection energy: vol(L,φ,ψ)=E(φ,ψ), in Boucksom–Eriksson’s normalization. Boucksom–Eriksson, 1805.01016v3, Theorem A.

Let X be a geometrically reduced projective scheme over an arbitrary complete non-Archimedean field, L and M ample line bundles, φ a continuous psh metric on L, and ψ₁,ψ₂ continuous psh metrics on M. Set f=ψ₁−ψ₂ and C=((L+M)ⁿ)−(Lⁿ). Then C inf f≤∫f(ddᶜφ+ddᶜψ₁)ⁿ−vol(L,φ+f,φ)≤C sup f. Boucksom–Gubler–Martin, Differentiability of relative volumes over an arbitrary non-Archimedean field, IMRN 2022, Lemma 3.2.
passages.quote: continuous psh metrics on an auxiliary ample line bundle M

passages.statement: For a geometrically reduced projective Berkovich space over a complete non-Archimedean field, the synthetic test space is generated by real PL/model functions and is uniformly dense in continuous functions; model forms and their mixed measures are given by numerical classes and intersection measures; positive Bott–Chern classes are the preimage of ample numerical classes. For a semipositive model form ω of ample class, rational psh PL tests are uniformly dense in Dω, Dω admits maxima, and the ordered tests φ<f satisfy limφ∫(f−φ)MAω(φ)=0 for every model test obstacle f. Boucksom–Jonsson, 2307.01697v1, Sections 1.2.2–1.3.2, Example 2.13, Definition 2.15 and Example 2.20.

In the synthetic model setting with ω≥0 of positive class, define MAω as the probability normalization, Jω(a,b)=Eω(a)−Eω(b)+∫(b−a)MAω(a), Jω(a)=Jω(0,a), Qω(ν)=supDω(Eω(a)−∫a dν), and rν(a)=Qω(ν)−Eω(a)+∫a dν. Test functions satisfy Jω(a,b)≈Jω(b,a), Jω(a,(1−t)a+tb)≤Cₙt²Jω(a,b), and Jω(a,b)≤Cₙ(rν(a)+rν(b)). If ω has orthogonality, Qω(ν)≤R and a,b,τ∈Dω have Jω≤R, then |∫(a−b)(dν−MAω(τ))|≤CₙJω(a,b)^αrν(τ)^(1/2)R^(1/2−α), α=2^(−n). Maximizing test sequences have MA measures converging strongly to ν. Boucksom–Jonsson, 2307.01697v1, Theorem 1.33, Proposition 2.2, Theorem 2.23 and Lemma 2.25.

For an irreducible projective Berkovich space over a complete non-Archimedean field and a semipositive model form ω of ample numerical class, there is a finite Tω such that sup a−∫a MAω(0)≤Tω for all a∈Dω. Boucksom–Jonsson, 2307.01697v1, Theorem 1.26 and the submean-value definition.

For a smooth connected projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, every nef numerical class has the envelope property. For an ample class, normalized PSH is compact, continuous-obstacle envelopes are continuous, and psh functions admit decreasing Fubini–Study regularization. Boucksom–Jonsson, 1801.08229v4, Theorem 4.15, Lemma 5.17, Theorem 5.20 and Corollary 5.21.

On a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, the intersection energy pairing for ample classes extends uniquely by decreasing psh majorants, is finite on finite-energy tuples, and has a symmetric multilinear finite-energy extension. It defines positive mixed Radon MA measures for psh tuples, of the mixed intersection mass, agreeing with model intersection measures and continuous along decreasing finite-energy nets. Finite-energy potentials are integrable against these measures; weighted measures also converge along decreasing integrable psh tuples. For an ample class, finite-energy locality and comparison hold. Boucksom–Jonsson, 1801.08229v4, Theorems 7.1, 7.8, 7.14 and 7.18, Propositions 7.19 and 7.21, and Theorems 7.40 and 7.44.

For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω, the dual energy supremum over finite-energy potentials equals the supremum over Fubini–Study tests; a Radon probability measure has finite dual energy exactly when it integrates every E¹ potential. For such a measure, convergent psh nets with eventually bounded J converge in L¹. If ω has the envelope property, then for every u∈E¹ and continuous f, the derivative at zero of Eω(Pω(u+tf)) is ∫f MAω(u). Boucksom–Jonsson, 1801.08229v4, Proposition 9.4, Proposition 9.19, Theorem 9.20, Theorem 8.5 and Corollary 8.6.

For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω, MA embeds E¹/R into the finite-dual-energy Radon probability measures. Surjectivity, the envelope property and completeness of E¹/R in its energy topology are equivalent. In particular, for smooth X in characteristic zero, every finite-dual-energy Radon probability measure is MA of an E¹ potential, unique modulo constants. Boucksom–Jonsson, 1801.08229v4, Proposition 12.7 and Theorems 12.8–12.9.

In the synthetic setting with a semipositive form ω of positive class satisfying orthogonality, the finite-dual-energy probability measures form a complete Dirichlet quasi-metric space, and its topology is their strong topology. This is a statement about the measure space. Boucksom–Jonsson, 2307.01697v1, Theorem 2.26.

For a smooth connected projective variety over a complete nontrivially discretely valued field of residue characteristic zero, and a closed real model (1,1)-form θ of ample numerical class, BFJ’s θ-psh cone is convex and stable under constants and maxima; divisorial evaluations determine its elements; its topology is pointwise convergence on divisorial points, equivalently uniform convergence on SNC dual complexes; u↦sup(u−ψ) is continuous and proper for every model ψ; normalized PSH is compact; decreasing nontrivial limits remain psh; every psh function has decreasing psh model regularization; continuous obstacles have continuous psh envelopes. On sufficiently high models, a bounded model change makes θ relatively ample, with arbitrarily small change when θ is semipositive. BFJ, 1201.0187v2, Propositions 5.2 and 7.4–7.9, Theorems 7.10–7.11, 8.3 and 8.7.
passages.quote: Endpoint D: complete nontrivially discretely valued residue-characteristic-zero K, smooth geometrically integral projective X, ample L, semipositive model reference; no function-field algebraizability, torus invariance, target support, or dimension-one restriction.

Boucksom–Jonsson, 1801.08229v4, Proposition 12.7 and Theorems 12.8–12.9.

In the synthetic setting with a semipositive form ω of positive class satisfying orthogonality, the finite-dual-energy probability measures form a complete Dirichlet quasi-metric space, and its topology is their strong topology. This is a statement about the measure space. Boucksom–Jonsson, 2307.01697v1, Theorem 2.26.
